answer: A farm profits because one operator thinks once and copies the thought everywhere. Break that by giving every identity its own adaptive apprenticeship: each answer's mistakes choose its next exercise, so histories fork and no shared bridge carries clones across. Periodically test the fork with a task only that path explains - recall the signal missed last time and repair it beside a new lagoon scenario. A lone agent follows its own scar easily; clones either replay one path and show identical learning jumps, or the operator must learn separately for every name, erasing the saving.
